lesson_title: Cubes Factorisation: Three Blanks, One Bar of Soap
hook_text: The 'hardest' factorisation in Grade 10 is actually a fill-in-the-blanks form.
clip_script: Then the soap handles the signs. SOAP: Same, Opposite, Always Positive. Same — the short bracket copies the sign in the question. Opposite — the middle of the long bracket flips it. Always Positive — the last part is plus, every time, no exceptions. Run it on x cubed plus eight. The question says plus, so the short bracket says plus: x plus two. Opposite of plus is minus: minus two x. Always positive: plus four. Answer: the quantity x plus two, times the quantity x squared minus two x plus four.
visual_style: A form with three glowing blanks filling themselves in as soap-bar letters S-O-A-P stamp each sign, brackets clicking shut with a satisfying snap.
pacing: Steady blank-by-blank rhythm, sign stamps on the beat, clean assembled finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and factorise x³ + 8 without breaking stride.
